title: Filtered-injective representatives and Hom computation in the filtered localization
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with enough injectives [def-sp-abelian, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Write $\operatorname{Fil}^f(\mathcal A)$ for objects with a finite decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration], and let $K_F^+(\mathcal A)$ be the homotopy category of bounded-below cochain complexes of these objects. Morphisms and chain homotopies preserve every filtration step; the graded complexes are the quotients $\operatorname{gr}^pK=F^pK/F^{p+1}K$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. Let $DF^+(\mathcal A)$ be its localization at chain maps inducing quasi-isomorphisms on all graded complexes. A filtered object is called filtered injective if all its graded objects are injective in $\mathcal A$; write $\mathcal I^f$ for their full additive subcategory. Every $K\in K_F^+(\mathcal A)$ admits a filtered quasi-isomorphism $K\to I$ with $I$ bounded below and termwise filtered injective. For every such $I$ and every bounded-below filtered complex $K$, localization induces a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{K_F^+(\mathcal A)}(K,I)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{DF^+(\mathcal A)}(K,I).$$
The canonical functor $K^+(\mathcal I^f)\to DF^+(\mathcal A)$ is an exact equivalence of triangulated categories. Forgetting the filtration and every $\operatorname{gr}^p$ send these representatives to bounded-below complexes of ordinary injectives and commute with the equivalence and the canonical functors to $D^+(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. All the assertions restrict to any fixed finite filtration interval $[a,b]$, meaning $F^aK=K$ and $F^{b+1}K=0$, with resolutions in that same interval.

proof.text: Use the bounded-below filtered-injective resolution theorem for the first conjunct.

Use the filtered acyclic-to-injective vanishing theorem and the distinguished-triangle exactness of the localized filtered homotopy category to show precomposition by every graded quasi-isomorphism is bijective. The localization left-fraction API then gives the Hom bijection by a denominator retraction.

The inclusion is full and faithful. Combining its map bijections with the localization Hom bijection gives full faithfulness of the comparison; resolutions and localization essential surjectivity give essential surjectivity.

Filtered injectivity of the underlying terms follows from the finite graded-filtration splitting theorem. The comparison is triangulated by the standard localization and full-subcategory instances. Termwise equality of evaluation functors descends through localization to the displayed comparison isomorphisms.
